text:
morgan: quick heads-up — thinking about a lighter fallback mode (working name: lite-mode) that returns a structured stub instead of a full generation when cost/latency triggers hit. want to sketch UX and telemetry before i wire it into the console.
arya: curious — is this intended for severe infra limits only, or also for noisy regressions where output quality drops?
devin: both. main idea: we expose 3 fallback outcomes: 1) full model swap (cheaper model), 2) truncated/partial response (lite-mode), 3) structured placeholder (no-generation) + hint. Lite-mode is a compromise: cheap, returns summary + pointers instead of full text.
srinivas: API-wise we should flag why we fell back. propose header: `X-Redwood-Fallback: reason=latency|error|quota;mode=lite|swap|placeholder;policy=v1` so clients can act deterministically.
arya: +1. For console UX, ops want to see "who/why" easily. How do we present lite-mode in the rollout UI? show it as a secondary rollout with its own traffic % and an audit sample?
morgan: exactly. UX sketch: rollout panel lists primary model and any fallback variants. each variant has toggles: sample rate for audit capture, visibility (public/private), and an explainability log link. clicking explainability opens a sampled request with: request headers, fallback reason, short diff between original and fallback output.
devin: telemetry: we must record both the triggering signal and the pre-fallback score if available (e.g., latency_ms, error_code, quality_metric). payload idea:

```
{ "ts": 4370001250, "req_id": "r-123", "fallback": "lite", "reason": "latency", "latency_ms": 1200, "primary_model": "redwood-a-2", "fallback_model": "lite-summary-v1", "sampled_output": "{...}" }
```

morgan: also capture aggregate counters per policy: total_requests, fallback_count, avg_latency_primary, avg_latency_fallback, sampled_quality_delta
srinivas: question about billing/quota: if we fall back to a cheaper model that counts differently, how do we show charges and quotas in usage dashboards? Should lite-mode consume 'fallback tokens' or map to same quota but cheaper unit?
arya: my vote is to surface both: keep customer-facing "consumed_units" with normalized units for cost, plus a raw_breakdown of underlying model units for transparency. console can show normalized cost + a per-variant breakdown link.
devin: operator case: we need an escape hatch to force-disable lite-mode for a customer (support+admin). UX: rollout row has an override button (sticky) and an audit trail entry: who toggled, reason, and commit id.
morgan: audit requirements: every fallback decision must be reproducible for forensic review. store the decision tuple: (policy_id, input_hash, model_candidates, metrics_at_time, chosen_variant). sample retention configurable per rollout (default 30d, enterprise 365d).
arya: threading with APIs: add `?explain=true` query for debug calls that returns the decision path (only for sampled/internal keys) — but ensure PII scrubbed in exported explain logs.
srinivas: implementation nit: avoid logging full user prompt in explain dumps — only hash + redacted prompt preview (first 64 chars) unless customer opts-in.
opsbot: deploybot: rollout-ui/feature/lite-mode feature flag turned on in staging at 4370001260 by ci-user.
devin: last ask — telemetry payloads should include a tiny snippet of fallback output + summary tokens so QA can compare quality. we can keep sampled_output small: max 512 chars.
morgan: ok next steps: i can mock a console wireframe and post sample API header + response stub schema. arya + srinivas want to sync on billing normalization. can we do 30m sync tomorrow 10am?
